clue.text: Criticised hit

definitions.meaning: to criticise sharply is to run down or disparage
to hit is to strike or rap

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit the one word: a knocked play was disparaged, and a knocked door was struck.

clue.text: Room where Kenneth contains his restless desire

indicators.note: contains says the short name holds the craving inside it

parts.note: Ken is short for Kenneth
an itch is a restless craving

explanation.surface: A man named Kenneth keeps his urges in check in one part of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' signals a container; 'his' is only a link joining Kenneth to his desire.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen is the room where food is cooked.

clue.text: Sequence of eleven?

parts.note: the number 11 written in figures is one digit 1 followed by another 1

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in succession, and 11 is literally a 1 then a second 1.

clue.text: Does it fly like a bird?

definitions.text: Does it fly like a bird?

parts.words: Does it fly like a bird?
parts.note: a toy flown on a string, which shares its name with a bird of prey

explanation.definitionFit: A kite is both a string-held toy aloft in the wind and a hawk-like raptor.

clue.text: Swindle of French/German woman on daughter

parts.note: de is French for of
Frau is German for woman or wife

explanation.surface: A Franco-German woman cheats her own daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To defraud someone is to cheat them out of money.

clue.text: Humorous magazine has nearly everything at the back

indicators.note: at the back places the shortened word after the magazine

parts.note: a comic is a magazine of cartoon strips

indicators.note: nearly says the word for everything stops one letter short

parts.note: everything means all

explanation.surface: A funny magazine supposedly carries everything in its final pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the last letter of the word for everything; 'at the back' sets that after the magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comical is funny, the same sense as humorous.

clue.text: Withhold information about six balls in a beaker

indicators.note: in places the cricket term inside the drinking vessel

parts.note: a cup is a drinking beaker
in cricket an over is six balls bowled

explanation.surface: Someone hides the truth about six balls kept in a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six deliveries from one bowler; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover up is to conceal facts, as in hiding a scandal.

clue.text: Can have a ball in Ireland

definitions.note: the definition places the answer as a county located in Ireland

parts.note: may means can, as in permission
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: Permission to attend a dance on the Emerald Isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' suggests a dance, but it is the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is a county on the west coast of the Irish Republic.

clue.text: Main route between England and France?

definitions.text: Main route between England and France?

parts.words: Main route between England and France?
parts.note: main is old poetic for the sea, so a sea passage across the strait between the two countries

explanation.definitionFit: Crossing the strait of Dover by ferry or tunnel is the usual sea trip from Dover to Calais.

clue.text: Caught young lady with nothing on, a journalist

parts.note: a lass is a girl
O is zero, nothing
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A naked girl was caught by a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lassoed an animal is to have caught it with a rope noose.

clue.text: Jubilee time

parts.note: a silver jubilee marks a quarter of a century, so the clue asks for that span spelt out

explanation.walkthrough: A jubilee is often a fiftieth anniversary, but the enumeration points to the silver one.
explanation.definitionFit: A silver jubilee celebrates an anniversary after a quarter-century has passed.

clue.text: Henry, towards the stern, finds a handle

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
aft means at or towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A man called Henry, going to the back of a boat, discovers a grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A haft is the grip or shaft of a knife, axe or tool.

clue.text: Transport vehicle by railway

parts.note: a car is a motor vehicle

explanation.surface: Goods are moved by a vehicle travelling on the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry something is to convey it from one place to another.

clue.text: Keen about the opening passage right away

indicators.note: away says the letter for right is sent off from the passage

parts.note: an intro is the opening passage of a piece of music or writing

explanation.surface: Someone enthusiastic about a piece's opening wants to hear it straight off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately', but 'away' removes R (right) from INTRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is informal for being enthusiastic about it.

clue.text: Not Alan falling in a dance

indicators.note: not says the short name is left out of the word falling

parts.note: Al is short for Alan

explanation.surface: Someone other than Alan takes a tumble on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes AL (Alan) from FALLING, its letters taken out in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A fling is a lively Scottish dance, as in the Highland version.

clue.text: Man in drivers' club in Turkey

definitions.note: the definition places the answer as a city found in Turkey

indicators.note: in places the man's name inside the motoring club

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motorists' organisation
Dan is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man belongs to a motorists' club in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a motoring organisation; the first 'in' is the container, the second a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adana is a large city in southern Turkey.

clue.text: Sharply provoked?

parts.note: read literally, provoked with something sharp, as pricked with a sewing point; the usual sense is irritated

explanation.definitionFit: To be needled is to be annoyed by persistent jibes, and a needle is literally sharp.

clue.text: Went barefoot in water or by canoe

definitions.meaning: walked about in shallow water with bare feet
moved a canoe along with a single-bladed oar

explanation.definitionFit: Wading in the shallows and propelling a small boat with an oar share the one verb.

clue.text: Longed for a new deanery

indicators.note: new says the letters of deanery are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone pined for a freshly built clergy residence.
explanation.definitionFit: To have yearned is to have wished intensely.

clue.text: Youth leader replaced trough containing curdled food

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of youth
replaced says the letters of trough are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A youth leader swaps a feeding trough for one holding curdled food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives Y, and 'replaced' rearranges TROUGH into OGHURT.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoghurt is milk fermented and thickened by bacteria.

clue.text: Decomposed for what sounded like ten years

indicators.note: what sounded like says the word is said aloud and heard as another

parts.note: a decade is ten years

explanation.surface: Something rotted away over what seemed a whole decade.
explanation.definitionFit: Decayed means rotted away, broken down by natural processes.

clue.text: Similar type and colour

parts.note: kind means a type or sort
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Two things alike in category and hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred spirits are alike in nature, so the word means alike or related.

clue.text: With the best sight and most eager

explanation.definitionFit: Keen means both sharp-sighted and enthusiastic, so the superlative covers each.

clue.text: Clothier from Wales?

definitions.meaning: a Welsh ... is a kitchen sideboard with shelves

explanation.walkthrough: A Welsh dresser is a traditional British piece of furniture, a sideboard topped with open shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: One who clothes others and a Welsh kitchen cupboard with plate shelves share the word.

clue.text: Turn on a fool

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone rounds on an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A goon is a stupid or clownish person.

clue.text: Debris forming an incomplete shield

indicators.note: incomplete says the word for shield loses its final letter

parts.note: a screen shields or protects

explanation.surface: Rubble piles up to make a partial barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts the last N from SCREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Scree is loose broken rock on a mountain slope.

clue.text: One's taking the Parisian area that's detached

parts.note: one is I, and the 's stays as S: I is
le is French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: Someone claims the Parisian region that has broken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives I plus S; 'the Parisian' asks for the French article LE.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is land cut off from the mainland by water, an island.

clue.text: Shop entrance features sign

indicators.note: features says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shop doorway displays a notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'features' signals the run hidden across 'Shop entrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice hung on a shop door announces that it is trading.

clue.text: Roman Catholics coming from tropics with a helmet

indicators.note: coming from says those letters are taken out of the word tropics

parts.note: RCs is short for Roman Catholics

explanation.surface: Catholics arrive from hot regions wearing a helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from' removes R, C and S (RCs, Roman Catholics) from TROPICS.
explanation.definitionFit: A topi is a lightweight sun helmet, also called a pith helmet.

clue.text: One isn't glad to recall such experiences

definitions.text: One isn't glad to recall such experiences

parts.words: One isn't glad to recall such experiences
parts.note: a description of past events whose recollection brings sorrow

explanation.definitionFit: Sad recollections are things a person would rather not bring to mind.

clue.text: Herd not stampeding whilst seated!

indicators.note: stampeding cattle scatter wildly, so the letters of herd not are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Cattle stay calm, not bolting, while sitting down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stampeding' rearranges HERDNOT; the definition means seated on a throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Throned means placed on a throne, a grand way of being seated.

clue.text: Catch agent setting off chain reaction

definitions.meaning: the catch on a gun that fires it
something that sets off a series of events

explanation.definitionFit: A gun's firing lever and an event that sparks a sequence of consequences share the word.
